newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 2.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* New economic data indicates that the nation's growth is easing to a more moderate pace, leading to expectations that the Fed policy makers will maintain current interest rates.
* Troubles at Viacom's Blockbuster continue, with the video store unit seeing earnings far below analyst expectations, forcing its parent company to take a $300 million write-down.
* The U.S. Postal Service wants to raise the cost of mailing a first-class letter by a penny to 33 cents.
* Rexall Sundown and TwinLab Corp said they are engaged in talks to merge.
* Two European drug makers, Amersham International Plc and Nycomed ASA, said they plan to merge.
* Chrysler reported a drop in sales for June of 4 percent.
* Program tradig has surged following the New York Stock Exchange's move to narrower stock-price increments.
* The U.S. Federal Trade Commission said it would not move to block Boeing's plan to acquire McDonnell Douglas.
* Stock funds rebounded in the most recent quarter, posting a gain of 15.3 percent, according to preliminary data.
* Pennzoil has rejected a hostile bid from Union Pacific Resources Group Inc.
* BellSouth plans to sell its stake in Australian telecommunications group Optus Communications Pty Ltd to Cable and Wireless Plc for $730 million.
* Motorola Inc plans to take a $170 million pre-tax charge against second-quarter earnings to phase out its limited participation in the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) market.
* Grupo Televisa SA is in the midst of a boardroom fight in the wake of the death of its chairman.
* The National Security Council and congressional auditors contend that auctioning certain airwaves for commercial wireless services could hinder U.S. military operations in the future.

* Heard on the Street: Takeover-stock traders were hit with big losses Tuesday on holdings of Office Depot, which saw its shares plummet 3-13/16, after a federal court ruling barred its proposed acquistion of Staples.
* Credit Markets: Weaker-than-expected economic figures gave nervous bond investors a reason to buy Treasury securities, leading to a rise in the market.
